Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
I had a pretty decent start in one of the rounds of the NC this year where I played a Nakthortheb Spell of Life deck.

From fourth position, I went
turn 1: Eternals of Sirius on Nakhthor, fish a vampire
turn 2: Eternals of Sirius on Nakthor, fish a vampire
turn 3: Villein Nakthor for 10, Giant's Blood, Play Spell of Life, untap, bleed prey for 1, play Enkil Cog

I went on to complete the spell on turn 7 and trash the table with 5 Inner Circle size-mummies.

The thing is, starts like this feel totally awesome, but are really not all that uncommon. People build their decks with the purpose to do exactly these things. An Alastor deck that can't Zillah out a fast Justicar and/or fails to pass the Alastor vote is useless, while it may look OMG WHAT AN AMAZING START if it actually does what it's designed to do.

What pushes some opening turns into the "this is ridiculous" territory is the whole Giant's crapshoot, but that's because Giant's Blood is broken.
